messages: want a script that exports last weeks readings to csv so i can look at them in a spreadsheet
I can write export_week.py using the Influx client: query the last 7 days for each sensor and write one CSV per sensor. Should it be a script, or part of the Rust bridge?
python, its a script, it runs once a week from cron. scripts are always python for me. the bridge stays rust obviously
Written: scripts/export_week.py, plus a cron line that runs it on Sundays at 18:00.
if i had the money id put smart valves on every radiator and get a heat pump, then hearth would be proper. but renting, so no
In a rented flat the sensible route is what you are doing: room sensors and a schedule on the existing boiler, with nothing fixed to the building.

title: How the notifier gets its events
messages: need to decide how notifier gets events from ingest now that its going in the monolith. options?

Three options. 1) A Postgres table used as a queue, polled with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. 2) RabbitMQ as a separate broker. 3) Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY to wake the notifier when rows arrive. The table is the simplest and durable; RabbitMQ gives more features at the cost of another service; LISTEN/NOTIFY is fast but does not store anything.

rabbit is another thing to run and monitor, no. listen/notify looses messages if the listener is down, which is exactly what bit us. polling table with skip locked. simple, durable, we already have postgres
Agreed. I will add an outbox table, and a notifier worker that claims rows with SKIP LOCKED and marks them done. Poll every 5 seconds to start.
5s ok to start. if people complain we can lower it
Implemented with tests, including two workers claiming rows at the same time.
great. so decision made: polling outbox table. rabbitmq out, listen/notify out
Recorded in the repository's decision log, with the three options and why two were rejected.
nice, future me will thank you

title: Dropping the cache
messages: i think we should drop the cache layer in atlas. it caused the stale tracking bug last week
Dropping the cache layer means removing the response cache middleware, the carrier-code lookup cache and the invalidation hooks in ingest. That removes all caching from Atlas. Proceed?
no, thats not what i meant. only the per request response cache goes. the carrier code lookup cache stays, it saves us a db hit on every event
Understood. I will remove only the per-request response cache middleware and its invalidation hooks. The carrier-code lookup cache stays, so ingest still uses it for every event.
yes. and add a note to the readme saying why: stale reads
Done. The README now says the response cache was removed in January because of stale tracking reads, and that the carrier-code cache remains.
perfect. im out this afternoon for an appointment, back friday

title: Dropping the 10k
messages: ok im calling it. im scrapping the 10k. the dog walks eat my evenings, its dark, and im behind on everything. ill skip it this year
That is a reasonable call. Dropping a goal on purpose is different from failing at it, and you can pick running up again whenever it suits you.
yeah no guilt. different thing: how long should a greyhound walk be? biscuit seems fine with 30 mins but pulls toward every squirrel
Thirty to forty-five minutes twice a day is typical. A well-fitted harness gives you more control than a collar for a dog with a narrow head.
Good. Let him sniff around the harness before the first walk so it is not strange to him.
he is the world's most suspicious dog about anything new, so yes

title: A flat in Bath
messages: big news, ive signed for a flat in bath. moving on saturday 7 feb. more space, a garden for biscuit

Congratulations. A short moving checklist: change your address with the bank and your employer, book broadband to start on the day, redirect your post, and register Biscuit's new address with the chip database.
the lease is 12 months. ill still work out of the bristol office so its a train in, about 40 mins
Forty minutes by train is a comfortable commute. A season ticket is usually cheaper than day returns if you go in three or more days a week.
yep. also the platform team thing at work, still going back and forth. ill think about it after the move
That is a sensible order. Big decisions are easier once the move is out of the way.
